page: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Edsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 768.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance includes 5669 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier status in PassMark CPU scores, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and single-threaded gzip compression both rank in the top 10% of benchmarks. While single-core stress-ng performance is average, multi-core stress-ng is strong. Memory bandwidth tests show top-tier read speeds for small cached blocks at 7496.51 GB/sec, and strong uncached read/write speeds for large blocks.

This hardware profile is highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive enterprise workloads due to its high resource density and local storage capacity. It excels in database operations, as evidenced by a top-tier Redis SET performance of 159.97 million operations per second and strong PassMark database scores. The presence of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions enables top-tier prompt processing speeds for small and medium LLM inference models, though text generation speeds remain average to strong. The server is highly suited for large-scale databases, memory-cached applications, and data-intensive enterprise workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Edsv7 family, powered by a 96-vCPU Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 768.0 GB of RAM, providing a high 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 5669 GB of local storage. The server delivers top-tier performance in PassMark CPU tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and cached memory bandwidth. It also achieves top-tier results in Redis SET operations at 159.97 million operations per second and static web serving throughput. While single-core CPU performance is average, its multi-core capabilities and advanced instruction sets, such as Intel AMX, make it highly efficient for memory-intensive workloads. This instance is optimized for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, and enterprise-grade data processing.
